discussion_comments.comment_body: AI Review: `result` contains only a count, so View Changes binds to the first item in the mutable global activity list. After completing a migration with older history, dismissing the new activity row leaves the result strip visible and promotes an older row to index 0; View Changes then opens unrelated paths. Store the created activity ID(s) in the result and resolve only those entries, or clear the action when they are dismissed.

AI Review: Skipped scopes retain their pending count, so with a completed profile and skipped workspace this line says some customizations need an update while the progress below counts the workspace as complete and reports `2 of 2 complete`. Derive both messages from the same included-pending predicate, or report skipped scopes separately.

Fixed in 479eb6bc98b (agent-assisted reply). The per-chat dedupe now uses `getSessionArtifactKey`, which compares files, websites and other URIs exactly. Only canonical GitHub PR/issue links ignore case and trailing slashes, and commit hashes ignore case. The pill-level `artifactValueKey` in `sessionArtifacts.ts` reuses the same key. A new regression test checks that `/repo/Report.md` vs `/repo/report.md` and `example.com/Docs?q=A` vs `/docs?q=a` stay separate.

This duplicates the earlier comment on the ordering constant. We intentionally preserve the known-level boundary: appending unknown values would use the fallback "Default permissions" metadata and produce a mislabeled row. Supported-but-withheld levels remain visible; unsupported levels stay hidden. A new built-in level must explicitly define its presentation and approval semantics.

*🤖 Authored with GitHub Copilot on behalf of @rwoll.*
